argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical defense of pragmatist metaethics against a charge of self-defeating incoherence
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate — premises are embedded in prose and reconstructed through examples and analogies

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High — engages directly with the strongest version of the objection and attempts to reframe the standard of evaluation
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High — all major moves bear on the coherence of Jamesian pluralism
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate — key premises depend on pragmatist commitments that critics may reject (e.g., no Archimedean point, dynamic coherence)

distinctions_drawn: External dogma vs. internal recursive meta-principle
explicit_definitions_given: Demand: any sentient striving or claim that creates moral value
Mutilation: necessary sacrifice of some demands for others
Melioristic universe: an unfinished world requiring cooperative action to improve

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges the force of the objection, then argues that the objection rests on a static misinterpretation of pragmatism
objections_raised: Talisse and Aikin's dilemma: arbitrariness or paralysis
Self-defeating tolerance: suppressing intolerance contradicts foundational hospitality to all demands
Thinness of Jamesian guidance in radical historical conflicts

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, thought experiments, economic analogy, textual interpretation
named_thought_experiments: Market analogy for primitive validity and regulation

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Defends Jamesian pragmatism while acknowledging genuine limits
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Metaethics, moral pluralism, tragic conflict, democratic inquiry

structural_organization.structure_type: Thesis-antithesis-synthesis with recursive refinement; introduction, five parts, conclusion

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that Jamesian moral philosophy is coherent if understood as an experimental, dynamic practice rather than a static algorithm. It reconstructs James's demand-based metaethics, presents the Talisse-Aikin dilemma, and resolves it by introducing a recursive meta-principle: tolerance and agency-preservation are internal conditions for the possibility of ongoing moral life. The conclusion is a qualified 'yes' to pluralistic coherence, with unresolved tensions around intolerance and radical conflict.
